missions.title: A real PM researches a strategy, pitches it, and the app's validation gates give a verdict the Human can read
missions.idea: The pitch, then a full report
missions.demo: uv run python acceptance/pitch_gates.py → ($0, offline) the gates first pass their controls (a planted-signal history passes, pure noise fails, the same strategy tried 1 time vs 200 times loses its deflated Sharpe); then the recorded real PM session replays IDENTICAL and prints the pitch: hypothesis, the strategy rule, every research backtest it ran (attempts counted), and the gate table on the held-out window with each number and PASS/FAIL/null
missions.notes: Plan session cycle 44. Slice 1 of 'The pitch and the gates' (Next up #1); serves the book ideas 'The pitch, then a full report', 'A strategy is an isolated function' and 'Validation gates before capital'. Shape decided by the plan (prime rule, refine in NOW.md): (1) a strategy is DATA, not code, in v1: a small versioned rule language (e.g. strategy-v1: signal momentum|mean-reversion|... with lookback, universe, rebalance every k days, top/bottom n, long-only|long-short, gross) evaluated by deterministic code in app/ as a pure function bars-up-to-t -> target weights. No agent code runs anywhere in v1 (agent-written code in a sandboxed subprocess is a later slice: seal work). (2) Research backtests: an endpoint + MCP tool; every call is an event, counted per pod forever (the deflated Sharpe's N cannot be hidden); research may only use bars up to today minus a held-out window. (3) The pitch: an endpoint + MCP tool with hypothesis text, data needed, the strategy rule, team and budget asked; physics runs the gates on the held-out window (still before today: the look-ahead guard holds) and records pitch_submitted + pitch_judged with every number. Gates: IC (mean rank IC and the number of predictions; per regime later), deflated Sharpe (Bailey & Lopez de Prado, N = the pod's attempts), capacity (simple impact vs the bars' volume), correlation with the other pods' return streams (null when there are none: null, not 0), hypothesis recorded but NOT judged by physics (no LLM in app/: the debate / backtest operator judges it, a later slice). Thresholds in config/laws, never hard-coded. v1 grants no capital (allocation is Next up #2): the verdict says 'eligible' or not. (4) Read side for the Human: GET /pitches, GET /pitches/{id} (+ MCP tools), shown in the demo. (5) Positive AND negative controls in the demo: the synthetic market is pure GBM (no signal), so every honest strategy should fail there; a gate that only rejects would pass a reject-only check, so the gate engine is also fed a planted-signal history (generated in the acceptance script, through the same pure functions) that must pass. (6) One real PM (Haiku 5.5 via OpenRouter, specs/pitch-desk/, small key) researches for a few sim-days and pitches; recorded once (cassette), replayed at $0 by the demo. OpenRouter credit ~$1.60 (2026-10-16). Risk tier: new permissions (who may backtest/pitch, pod-scoped) in app/registry/permissions.py + a real spend run -> red-team + auditor before merge. An ADR for the strategy language and the gate law. Left out: agent code in a sandbox, backtest operator, bull/bear debate, capital granted, IC per regime, factor attribution. Merged cycle 46 (3 build sessions): red-team 4 holes (2 fixed, 2 written down), auditor BLOCK (pod-less reader) fixed.

missions.notes: Dropped 2026-10-16 (Builder v3, ADR-046): re-cut into the ideas book, idea "Who hosts the agents: OpenClaw or the app's own runtime" (bible/IDEAS_BOOK.md). Raw material for that idea. Earlier notes: Raw material: BACKLOG R-7 (B-012, B-012a, B-012b, B-023s seal keys, B-000l loopback MCP URL); OCT POC charters → AgentSpec templates (08 §6). Rule zero first: verify every command and file name against the installed version (/opt/homebrew/bin/openclaw), pin it in runtime/openclaw/VERSION_NOTES.md. Rule one: never touch the Human's ~/.openclaw or any non-firm- agent; backup under umask 077 before the first change. The Builder's Bash sandbox can write only the repo and $TMPDIR: the architect must first verify whether the installed OpenClaw can keep a profile's state/config under a directory we choose (env or flag). If yes, the acceptance check renders + applies + doctors inside a temp dir. If no, split by capability: (a) render + every static check that reads only rendered artifacts, run in a temp dir; (b) apply to ~/.openclaw-firm as a step the Human runs once (question in state/QUESTIONS.md). The acceptance check must skip nothing silently: if `openclaw` is absent it FAILS (it is installed here). Gate change 'no conformance → no wake' → RED-TEAM: yes. Live probes stay skipped while the cap is null (Q-0001).

missions.title: Physics refuses instead of crashing, and a run it will refuse leaves no trace: the 9 open strict xfails pass
missions.question: Are the known physics holes closed before minds that register, message and trade at small size arrive (before vision M6 / R-8)?
missions.demo: uv run python acceptance/M-004.py → lists each of the 9 hole tests (red-team 0001 ×3, 0004 ×1, 0009 ×2, 0020 ×3) and PASS for each, with xfail markers removed; plus a live App: register into a missing pod → 404/409, not 500
missions.notes: Dropped 2026-10-16 (Builder v3, ADR-046): re-cut into the ideas book, idea "Known physics holes" (bible/IDEAS_BOOK.md). Raw material for that idea. Earlier notes: Bundle: B-056 (+B-019, same root: register with a missing/absent pod → 500; fix in app.registry.service.register_agent), B-055 ×2 (_conduct reads /agents + pods + published tool list before declare_minds), B-000g ×2 (byte caps on structured_payload and task outcome), B-000e (message body + structured_payload on message_sent), B-026 (fee under $5 notional pays $0.00 — a fee-law change: ADR), B-036 ×2 (OMS_LOCK per process; cross-process advance vs fill). B-036 may be larger than the rest: the architect may cut it to its own later mission or accept it by ADR with its reason (Art. 9: a hole accepted is written, never hidden). Acceptance runs the named tests with the markers gone (it fails today because they xfail). New red-team lows found during M-001..M-003 land here. RED-TEAM: yes. From M-001's red-team (tests/test_redteam_0021.py, 3 strict xfails; ADR-044): (medium) mid-run leaderboard ranks metered minds on self-report until the one sync - fix = post every key at 0 after provision, which needs the trailing-block compare-ledgers law written with it; (medium) inbox-stuffing drains a metered mind's key - per-sender message quota (law change, ADR); (low) a part-way sync failure reports posted 0 and counts every key unattributed. Also (auditor, c38): now that the Human set a cap and left a provisioning key (Q-0001/2 answered 2026-10-15), ADR-044 §4 'monthly accounting across runs before any real key' must become a check in code before any real provider name joins METERED_PROVIDERS - with B-022 (secret scan).

missions.title: A Truman shock: a scenario file crashes a market on day d of a keyed synthetic month, `system` announces it, a pod lives through it, and the same key + scenario replays to the same ledger
missions.question: Can the world script events — the lever by which the Builder changes the world without touching a mind (Art. 10) — deterministically and on the record? (Era I deliverables 4–5: Truman v1 + world events; prerequisite of Era II EC2)
missions.demo: uv run fund-runtime backtest --specs specs/desk-month --steps 31 --scenario scenarios/crash-day-12.yaml → day 12: a `world_event` + `system` announcement in the ledger, the shocked ticker's close drops by the scenario's amount, the scripted pod's equity curve shows it; run twice → compare-ledgers IDENTICAL
serves: Era I deliverable 4 (Truman v1, synthetic half)
missions.notes: Dropped 2026-10-16 (Builder v3, ADR-046): re-cut into the ideas book, idea "Market shocks as world events" (bible/IDEAS_BOOK.md). Raw material for that idea. Earlier notes: Raw material: B-007 (world events table + system announcements), B-008 (Truman v1). Built on the keyed synthetic market (ADR-030), not on a real-history pack: fetching real history needs network the Builder's sandbox does not have (the real-history pack is a later mission or a one-time command the Human runs). The scenario is part of the run's world (ADR-031: run_started.world records it; agents see 'withheld' per ADR-034, the announcement is what they are told). The look-ahead guard holds: no agent learns of a shock before its day. Whether an agent is told its data is synthetic is an experimental variable (08 §4) — record it per run. RED-TEAM: yes (marketdata).

missions.title: Central risk acts by law: a pod driven down by a Truman crash has its capital cut at 5% drawdown, goes reduce-only at 7.5% and is liquidated and closed at 10% — exactly, on the record
missions.question: Can physics enforce the firm's risk ladder (04_FIRM §5) deterministically, so a pod's death is a law, not a judgement? (Era II EC2: 'a forced-drawdown Truman scenario triggers 5% / 7.5% / 10% actions exactly')
missions.demo: uv run python acceptance/M-006.py → a scripted pod lives a month with a 3-step crash scenario; prints the high-water mark, each threshold crossing (day, drawdown %), the ledger event for each action, a refused new-risk order after 7.5% (403/409 + event), and the pod closed with zero positions after 10%
missions.notes: Dropped 2026-10-16 (Builder v3, ADR-046): re-cut into the ideas book, idea "The central risk ladder" (bible/IDEAS_BOOK.md). Raw material for that idea. Earlier notes: Starts Era II while Era I's real-mind criteria wait on the Human's cap (ADR-043). 04_FIRM §5: drawdown from the pod's high-water mark within the generation; 5% → allocation cut to 50%, positions above the new limit reduced within 2 sim-days or by the OMS; 7.5% → reduce-only (+ mandatory review workflow: record the event only, the CRO/CEO workflow is a later mission); 10% → liquidated, closed for the generation. Firm-level 8%/12% and exposure limits: out of scope (next mission). Reuse app/metrics/equity.py and the OMS; every action is an event, derived state rebuildable from the ledger. RED-TEAM: yes (oms).
